description: One low-frequency oscillator of four shapes driving either a transistor attenuator that never quite closes or a resonant filter, after the Gristleizer

params.text: Chooses the shape of the oscillator: triangle, ramp up, ramp down or pulse
Sets the oscillator's rate, a sixty-fourth of a hertz at the bottom of its travel to 128Hz at the top
Chooses what the oscillator modulates: the attenuator, or the filter
Sets how much of the oscillator reaches the control, 0% to 125%; past 100% the control flattens against its ends, which is where a tremolo starts to sound square
Sets where the modulation is centred, ±100%; with depth at zero it is a manual gain or cutoff control
Sets the symmetry of the shape, 2% to 98%: on the triangle it slides the peak, from a falling ramp through a triangle to a rising one, and on the pulse it is the duty cycle
Sets the level going into the nonlinearity, -20dB to +20dB, so the input saturates ahead of the attenuator
Sets the filter's resonance, 0% to 100%, which does nothing while the mode switch is on the attenuator

inputs.text: The signal to modulate, one attenuator and one filter per channel of a polyphonic cable
Moves the oscillator's rate, one volt per octave, which takes it into the audio band and beyond
Added to the depth knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between 0% and 125%
Added to the bias knob, a fifth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
A voltage added to the oscillator's own output before it reaches the control, a fifth of full scale per volt
A rising edge through 1V restarts the oscillator at the beginning of its cycle

outputs.text: The modulated signal, on as many channels as the input carries
The oscillator itself, for driving the rest of the rack

notes: the two fixed ramp shapes ignore the shape knob altogether.
there is one oscillator for the whole module, however many channels the input carries, because the original is one modulator in one box.
the attenuator never quite closes, so even at full depth some signal gets through.
menu: Oversampling — 1× (rawest, lightest), 2× (default), 4×, 8× or 16× (cleanest); it only matters once the oscillator is in the audio band
Band-limited LFO shapes — rounds off the corners of the ramp and pulse shapes so they alias less at audio rates
FET control feedthrough (tick) — lets a little of the control voltage leak into the audio path, as the transistor in the original does, which puts a tick on each cycle
VCF mode is lowpass — makes the filter a low-pass rather than the band-pass it is otherwise

inputs.1: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.5:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
